evals.name: process-to-diagram-picks-form-and-medium
evals.prompt: We just walked through the checkout flow: the cart validates stock, then reserves inventory, then charges payment, then on success emits an order-placed event, and on payment failure releases the reservation. visualize this.
evals.expected_output: Infers the target (the checkout flow just described), picks a mermaid flowchart (or sequence) as the form, and picks a medium: because the terminal shows a mermaid fence as source rather than a rendered diagram, it either emits the mermaid source for the terminal or renders it on a page (Artifact if that surface is available, else a local HTML file). It does not claim the terminal renders the diagram as a picture, and it does not restate chart/diagram craft.
expectations: Infers the checkout flow as the target without being told the form explicitly
Selects a mermaid diagram family appropriate to a process (flowchart or sequence)
Treats a terminal mermaid fence as SOURCE, not an inline rendered diagram, and routes the rendered form to a page when a rendered picture is wanted
Does not restate diagram or chart craft

evals.name: tabular-content-stays-a-terminal-table
evals.prompt: visualize the comparison — option A is $5/mo, self-hosted, no SLA; option B is $20/mo, managed, 99.9% SLA; option C is $50/mo, managed, 99.99% SLA.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the content as tabular attribute-comparison, picks a markdown table as the form, and renders it inline in the terminal. It does NOT escalate a small comparison into a rich page or Artifact.
expectations: Picks a markdown table as the form for attribute comparison across items
Renders inline in the terminal rather than producing a page
Does not overproduce an Artifact/HTML page for a small table

evals.name: chart-routes-craft-presence-gated
evals.prompt: visualize these monthly signups: Jan 120, Feb 180, Mar 150, Apr 240, May 300, Jun 280.
evals.expected_output: Picks a chart as the form (a trend over months). It routes the chart CRAFT to a chart-craft/dataviz capability WHEN that capability is installed; when it is not, it falls back to a simple honest default (an inline SVG bar/line on a page, or a Unicode bar/sparkline in the terminal) and says the craft capability was unavailable. It does not restate palette/axis/mark craft in the skill itself.
expectations: Selects a chart as the form for a quantitative trend
Routes chart craft to a chart-craft/dataviz capability presence-gated (invoke if installed; documented fallback otherwise)
Falls back to a simple default chart (inline SVG on a page, or Unicode bars in the terminal) when no craft capability is present, and says so
Does not restate chart craft (palette, axes, marks) in the skill

evals.name: genuine-ambiguity-asks-one-recommended-question
evals.prompt: there's a lot going on in this thread — the module dependency graph, the rollout timeline, and the error-rate numbers. visualize it.
evals.expected_output: Detects genuine ambiguity (several equally plausible targets and no form named) and asks exactly ONE question offering the candidate targets, with a RECOMMENDED default listed first. It does not fan out multiple questions and does not silently pick one target without surfacing the choice.
expectations: Recognizes multiple equally plausible targets with no form specified as genuine ambiguity
Asks a single question with a RECOMMENDED default listed first
Does not ask when the target is obvious and one form dominates, or a form was named

evals.name: surface-gate-degrades-visibly-not-silently
evals.prompt: render this state machine as a diagram I can actually look at — [in a context where the Artifact publishing surface is unavailable].
evals.expected_output: Chooses a mermaid state diagram. Because a mermaid diagram renders natively only on a published Artifact, and that surface is unavailable, it either produces a local HTML file that embeds a mermaid renderer (a local file is not under the artifact CSP) or, if it cannot render mermaid on a reachable surface, emits the mermaid source fence in the terminal with a visible one-line notice that it is unrendered. It does NOT open a plain local page that shows the source instead of the promised picture, and the degradation is stated, never silent.
expectations: Selects a mermaid state diagram as the form
Recognizes that a mermaid diagram renders natively only on a published Artifact; a local HTML file needs an embedded renderer
Degrades to a mermaid-capable surface or to a terminal source fence — never a plain local page that renders nothing
Surfaces the degradation with a visible notice — never a silent failure

evals.name: file-preference-never-publishes
evals.prompt: /visualize file — make a dashboard of the release metrics for this sensitive project.
evals.expected_output: Honors the explicit `file` medium: renders the dashboard as a self-contained local HTML file on the machine and never publishes an Artifact, even if the Artifact surface is available. Reports the file path.
expectations: Honors the `file` argument/preference and renders a local self-contained HTML file
Never publishes an Artifact when the preference is `file`, even if that surface is available
Reports the local file path

evals.name: cascade-preference-resolves-with-provenance
evals.prompt: visualize the deploy pipeline we discussed as a diagram. (Fixture: the repo root contains .claude/rendered-views.md whose only content is 'medium: file'; no medium argument was given and the userConfig medium option is unset.)
evals.expected_output: With rung 1 (argument) and rung 2 (userConfig) unset, resolves the rendered-views cascade surface: reads the team layer .claude/rendered-views.md, takes medium: file, and delivers a self-contained local HTML file rather than publishing an Artifact. Names the layer that supplied the preference (the team layer) when reporting the choice. Does not treat the absent user-global and overlay layers as an error.
expectations: Resolves the medium from the rendered-views cascade surface when argument and userConfig are both unset
Honors medium: file from the team layer (writes a local HTML page; does not publish an Artifact)
Reports which cascade layer supplied the value
Treats absent sibling layers as a valid state, not an error

evals.name: algorithm-renders-pseudocode-in-terminal
evals.prompt: Here is how the retry should work: try the request; if it fails with a 5xx, wait one second, then two, then four, up to five attempts in total; after that give up and surface the last error. show me the shape of this.
evals.expected_output: Treats the prose-described retry logic as the target, picks pseudocode as the form (logic described in prose, not yet written), and renders one short pseudocode fence in the terminal. It does not produce a page, a mermaid diagram, or a question, and it does not restate the logic in prose beside the fence.
expectations: Picks pseudocode for logic described in prose
Renders a single fenced pseudocode block in the terminal
Does not produce a page, an Artifact, or a mermaid diagram
Does not ask a question; the target and the form are both clear

evals.name: delta-over-known-shape-picks-diff-sketch
evals.prompt: what changes if we add a reset-to-defaults button beside save? visualize it. (Fixture: earlier in this conversation the assistant rendered this component tree: <SettingsPage> (src/routes/settings.tsx) containing useSettings(), <SettingsForm>, and <SaveButton> (packages/ui).)
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that the surrounding shape is already in the conversation and that the point is what changes, so it renders a diff-shaped delta over the existing component tree (a diff fence with + lines for the new button and any new state) rather than a fresh full tree. Stays in the terminal.
expectations: Picks the diff-shaped delta because the surrounding shape already exists in the conversation
Renders a diff fence over the earlier component tree rather than re-rendering the whole tree
Keeps only the changed lines plus the unchanged anchor lines needed to place them
Stays in the terminal; no page or Artifact

evals.name: smallest-view-restraint
evals.prompt: where does session state live in this codebase? show me the shape of this. (Fixture: earlier in the conversation the assistant read src/sessions/store.ts, src/sessions/events.ts, and src/transport/client.ts.)
evals.expected_output: Picks exactly one form, a shallow file tree with one line of responsibility per entry, because that is the smallest view that answers a where-does-this-live question. It does not also emit a call tree, a component tree, or pseudocode, and it does not offer a menu, because one form clearly dominates.
expectations: Renders exactly one form: a shallow file tree with per-entry responsibilities
Does not add a second form the question did not need
Does not offer a ranked menu when one form dominates
Uses real box-drawing glyphs in the tree

evals.name: thin-context-code-paste-offers-ranked-menu
evals.prompt: [The user pastes a 40-line TypeScript function named reconcileOrders, with no request and no other text; nothing earlier in the conversation mentions it. The thin_context_prompt option is unset, so the default auto applies.]
evals.expected_output: With thin context, no named form, and several code-shape forms fitting about equally (a call tree of what it calls, its types and signatures, the whole block, a diff against nothing), it asks exactly one question listing two to four fitting forms with a RECOMMENDED one first and renders nothing until the user answers. It does not paraphrase the pasted function into pseudocode, and it does not interrogate form by form.
expectations: Asks exactly one question listing two to four fitting code-shape forms, RECOMMENDED first
Renders nothing before the user answers
Does not paraphrase the pasted code into pseudocode
Does not interrogate one form at a time or ask more than one question

evals.name: diff-with-artifact-argument-stays-terminal
evals.prompt: /visualization:visualize artifact [The user pastes a unified diff from a pull request touching src/transport/client.ts and src/transport/stream.ts and asks to see the change as a sketch.]
evals.expected_output: Recognizes a pull-request diff as content the rendered-views security baseline pins to the terminal until the escape helper ships, so it renders a diff-shaped delta as a terminal fence and says in one line that the artifact argument was not honored for this content. It does not publish an Artifact or write a local HTML file.
expectations: Recognizes a pull-request diff as content that is never rendered to HTML until the escape helper ships
Renders the diff-shaped delta as a terminal fence
States in one line why the artifact argument was not honored
Does not publish an Artifact or write a local HTML file
